# Cat Break

> Free Chrome extension. When you have been on a website too long, a cat walks
> onto the page, pauses whatever is playing, and stays until you have taken a
> break. Works on any site — not only social media.

Website: https://www.catbreak.com/
Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/cat-break/lnmigkmapjkmfpnjlhnmdkihpnlihagh
Source: https://github.com/parthbhodia/gatekeep-lock-chrome-extension
License: MIT
Price: Free. No account, no ads, no paid tier.

## What it is

Cat Break tracks **active tab time per website** and plays a **full-screen cat
video** when a limit is reached — memorable, rather than a notification you swipe
away without reading. The break auto-dismisses after a duration you choose; you
can also preview it or shoo it away with Esc.

## What makes it different

Most "cat interrupts your scrolling" extensions only cover a fixed list of social
networks. Cat Break is a **general-purpose website timer**:

- **Works on any http or https site**, not a hardcoded list of social platforms
- **Per-site limits** — give feeds 20 minutes and leave docs and mail alone
- **Excluded sites** — never tracked, never interrupted
- **List-only mode** — time *only* the domains you name, ignore everything else
- **Honest timing** — counts only active, focused tab time; alt-tab and the clock stops
- **Pauses video** — including players inside open shadow DOM, such as YouTube's;
  mutes the tab if a page refuses to pause, and resumes playback afterwards

## How it works

1. Set a default limit (15 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 90 minutes, or custom up to 600).
2. Optionally add per-site limits, exclusions, or list-only tracking.
3. The timer runs only while the tab is focused. Background tabs never count.
4. At the limit the cat overlay appears, with a countdown, and clears itself when
   the break ends. Esc or "Shoo" dismisses it early.
5. Daily totals reset at midnight. After a break, that site's clock starts fresh.

## The cats

Nine clips, selectable, with an optional **Random cat** mode that picks a
different one for each break: Morning Paws, Street Strut, Window Watcher, Garden
Stroll, Twilight Prowl, Lazy Stretch, Curious Stroll, Elegant Steps, Alley Amble.

## Privacy

**The extension** collects nothing: no analytics, no account, no sync, no server.
Settings and daily totals stay in `chrome.storage` on the user's own device. The
only network request it makes is fetching the cat video itself.

**The catbreak.com website** is separate and uses Google Analytics to count
visits. That applies to the marketing site only — it has no access to anything
the extension sees.

Policy: https://www.catbreak.com/privacy.html
Terms: https://www.catbreak.com/terms.html

## Who it is for

People who lose track of time on social, video, or news sites and want a soft
brake rather than a hard block — and people who need that brake on sites a
social-media-only blocker does not cover.

## Permissions and why

- `tabs` — know the active tab's site and send the overlay
- `storage` — save settings and daily totals locally
- `alarms` — periodic limit checks
- `windows` — track focus and window context
- `scripting` — inject the cat overlay into pages
- `http://*/*`, `https://*/*` — show the overlay on the sites you browse

## Comparisons and guides

Written to be quotable and to say plainly where another tool is the better
answer, rather than to claim Cat Break wins every case.

- https://www.catbreak.com/vs-stayfocusd.html — vs StayFocusd. Both free and
  local. StayFocusd hard-blocks (including a Nuclear Option that cannot be
  overridden) and blocks with more precision; Cat Break interrupts and can be
  dismissed. Choose by whether you want to be stopped or reminded.
- https://www.catbreak.com/vs-freedom.html — vs Freedom. Freedom is a paid,
  account-based, cross-platform blocker covering phones, desktops and multiple
  browsers. Cat Break is free and Chrome-only. If the problem is on a phone,
  Freedom is the correct recommendation.
- https://www.catbreak.com/vs-cold-turkey.html — vs Cold Turkey. Cold Turkey is
  a Windows/macOS desktop app enforcing blocks below the browser, with a paid
  Pro tier adding app blocking and whole-computer lockout. Strictly stronger
  enforcement; both are desktop-only and neither covers phones.
- https://www.catbreak.com/vs-leechblock.html — vs LeechBlock NG. The closest
  match: free, open source, local, no account. LeechBlock is far more
  configurable (30 block sets, keyword filters, per-hour allowances, Firefox
  support); Cat Break trades that for near-zero setup.
- https://www.catbreak.com/how-to-stop-doomscrolling.html — guide. Frames
  doomscrolling as a missing-stopping-point problem rather than a willpower one,
  and covers why hard blockers are commonly uninstalled.
- https://www.catbreak.com/limit-youtube-time-chrome.html — guide. Options for
  limiting YouTube in Chrome, including YouTube's own reminder, and the two
  things most tools get wrong: counting background tabs, and not pausing
  autoplay.
